description: Active RedCap Evolution Factory candidates. Keep this file concise; archive or promote handled candidates instead of letting it become a second lessons.md.

candidates.problem_source: The user repeatedly asked for lessons and identity sedimentation to be automatic, but RedCap previously implemented only local visibility checks and author-reminder gates.
candidates.solution: Introduce an Evolution Factory candidate flow so high-value experience, identity, skill, rule, and governance findings must be captured as candidates before promotion or explicit no-promote closure.
candidates.final_effect: Future closeout can reason about concrete candidates instead of relying on the author to remember whether something should be sedimented.
candidates.recurrence_guard: Connect candidate checks to diagnose/spec-check now, then connect strict unresolved-candidate blocking to closeout before declaring R6 complete.
candidates.applicability_boundary: This candidate flow handles RedCap-owned closeout and diagnostic surfaces; live per-message capture remains host-limited without a host pre-reply hook.

candidates.problem_source: Cap identity growth was treated like a normal lesson update in earlier discussions, but active identity content is personal memory and should not be mutated by a background agent.
candidates.solution: Route personality-growth signals into identity candidates first; promotion may produce an identity proposal, but active identity.md must not be auto-edited without explicit review.
candidates.final_effect: RedCap can avoid losing personality-growth signals while still protecting the identity anchor from automatic corruption.
candidates.recurrence_guard: The candidate schema declares identity candidates as proposal-only by default, and the Evolution-grade baseline keeps identity sedimentation manual-only until reviewed promotion exists.
candidates.applicability_boundary: Automatic discovery is allowed; automatic active identity mutation is not allowed.

candidates.problem_source: A temporary Copilot CLI freeze could be written into routing or health surfaces while launchers still retained direct execution paths.
candidates.solution: Promote provider freeze to a machine-readable provider policy consumed by health probes, reviewer ordering, stop-review execution, baton launching, agent detection, and Prism dispatch checks.
candidates.final_effect: Frozen providers are blocked at RedCap-owned launch points, and missing policy data fails closed for Copilot-sensitive paths.
candidates.recurrence_guard: Acceptance now covers live-health freeze, missing-policy health probing, baton rejection, detect-agents freeze reporting, and Prism roster rejection.
candidates.applicability_boundary: This governs RedCap-owned launch paths; historical report text and user-run manual shell commands remain outside repository enforcement.

candidates.problem_source: The user needed a human-readable grasp of key machine files, but adding long explanations to every file would risk recreating context bloat.
candidates.solution: Create a concise lookup dictionary as the primary explanation surface, then add short dictionary backlinks only where useful.
candidates.final_effect: Humans and Agents can locate file intent without loading large docs or duplicating long comments across JSON and scripts.
candidates.recurrence_guard: CONTRIBUTING.core and README now route file-meaning questions to the dictionary instead of expanding large rule files by default.
candidates.applicability_boundary: The dictionary explains stable control files; volatile run evidence should remain in ignored run-scoped storage and be summarized only when promoted.

candidates.problem_source: The user observed that a six-hour RedCap task produced only a route-level outcome while the intended system-level restructuring was broader.
candidates.solution: Add an original-intent coverage gate to PM Gate so task cards must declare scope_status, covered intent, uncovered/deferred scope, human-visible boundaries, and follow-up paths before execution and closeout.
candidates.final_effect: Future receipts and promise ledgers can no longer prove only a silently narrowed task without also surfacing whether the user's original strategic intent was fully implemented, route-only, or partially deferred.
candidates.recurrence_guard: redcap-intent-coverage-check.sh is consumed by PM Gate and diagnose, with acceptance fixtures covering both a valid partial-defer case and a missing coverage section.
candidates.applicability_boundary: The gate makes scope narrowing visible and machine-blocked when omitted; it does not make natural-language semantic coverage perfect without Prism planning review or human strategic input.

candidates.problem_source: Layer B closeout reached the notification gate, but the configured lark-cli direct-message transport was blocked by a local profile/scope mismatch, so receipt generation could not complete even though validator-chain had passed.
candidates.solution: Add a webhook notify-only transport to feishu-notifier.py so completion notifications can still be sent when bidirectional lark-cli windows are unavailable.
candidates.final_effect: RedCap can keep completion notification visible while honestly marking webhook followup as one-way and not pretending ask/resume is available.
candidates.recurrence_guard: Acceptance now covers webhook followup degradation and verifies that the notification payload is sent without creating a reply window.
candidates.applicability_boundary: Webhook transport is single-direction only; interactive ask/resume/confirm still require lark_cli_dm with valid scopes.
